st.headline: Palm oil stocks tumble as S’pore looks for firms responsible for haze: Markets this week
st.teaser: ST’s business correspondents unpack the latest developments in the markets during the week and explain what they mean for investors.
fullText: SINGAPORE – The worsening haze across Singapore in recent weeks has cast a pall over the skies and certain stocks.
Palm oil shares took a tumble when some Singapore-listed companies were linked to plantation areas in Indonesia where fires and smoke were detected.
Prime Minister Lawrence Wong also said on Facebook on Oct 15 that Singapore is looking into which companies may be responsible for haze-causing fires.
He added that Singapore will take action under its Transboundary Haze Pollution Act and explore joint action with other countries, where warranted.

The law, which was enacted in 2014, targets those responsible for causing or condoning fires if the haze causes the Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) to stay in the unhealthy range in any part of Singapore for 24 hours or more.
Air quality is considered unhealthy when PSI levels are 101 and above. The PSI levels have been over 200 in some areas over the last few days.

Agribusiness group Wilmar International and palm oil company Golden Agri Resources were among the Singapore-listed firms that have addressed their involvement in the ongoing forest fires in Indonesia.
In response to queries on Oct 16 from the Singapore Exchange Regulation, both said that they have no-burning policies in place.
Golden Agri said that it “is not aware of information indicating that its operations or activities have caused or contributed to the recent transboundary haze”.

Wilmar said that it has not undertaken any new oil palm planting in its plantations in Indonesia since 2013. Since then, the firm’s field activities in Indonesia “have been limited to the replanting of existing planted areas, which is carried out mechanically and without the use of fire”.
Meanwhile, palm oil company Bumitama Agri said that some of its operations in Indonesia were affected by fires spread from surrounding land.

In a Singapore Exchange filing on Oct 16 evening, it said that based on internal observations and preliminary investigations, “no evidence has been established linking the Group’s operations with initiation of the fires under investigations and to the haze in question”.
The firm, which had earlier called for a trading halt, was named in an investigation by environmental group Greenpeace along with Singapore-listed palm oil company First Resources.
First Resources on Oct 15 said the fires detected within its Indonesian palm oil concessions were largely caused by external blazes spreading across its boundaries.
Privately held company First Borneo Plantations, which has ownership links to Singapore-incorporated companies, was also named in the Oct 5 report.

The report identified plantation concessions associated with the three companies where fires and smoke were detected between August and September. A concession grants a company the right to use or develop an area of land.
Wilmar’s shares closed 1.2% down on Oct 16, while Golden Agri-Resources saw shares tumble 3.5%.
First Resources saw shares fall by nearly 7%.
Bumitama Agri’s prices fell by 4.8% before the company requested for a trading halt before the afternoon session.
In a quirk of timing, fire-protection specialist Deluge started trading on the SGX mainboard on Oct 16.
The gross proceeds from the offering and cornerstone tranche are about $23.4 million. After deducting listing expenses, net proceeds are expected to be about $20.1 million.

Deluge said it plans to use the proceeds to invest in infrastructure, facilities and operational capabilities, pursue strategic partnerships through installations and lifecycle services, and strengthen its integrated fire-detection platform.
Deluge opened at $0.63 and closed 6.7% higher on its first trading day at $0.64.
Tech stocks started to show signs of recovery on Friday after a six-day rout that wiped some US$1.6 trillion off global semiconductor stocks.

Hott er-than-expected US inflation data stoked fears of further Federal Reserve rate hikes, along with unease over AI investment, causing the S&P 500 to fall 1.11% – its largest margin since July – while Asia n markets also tumbled.
Investors have questioned whether companies borrowing heavily to build AI infrastructure can generate enough cash to service their debts.
Chief executive Hock Tan of semiconductor and infrastructure software company Broadcom added fuel to the fire at a DBS AI event here on Oct 12 when he likened AI investors to gambling in a casino.

Asian markets, however, recovered ground on Oct 16, with South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index jumping nearly 4%, after falling over 7% the day before. Japan’s Nikkei also rose nearly 2%, after falling 5% on Oct 15.

US Federal Reserve boss Kevin Warsh also buoyed tech sentiment by saying he believed AI was the most consequential change to the global economy, predicting positive effects even though the path forward might be “bumpy”.

Speaking at the International Monetary Fund (IMF)-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok on Oct 16, he said AI would bring “huge benefit” to the global economy, although the investment boom would drive prices up in the short term.

cna.headline: Malaysia’s BN to announce candidates for Melaka polls on Oct 28: State chairman
cna.teaser: Ab Rauf Yusoh, who is also Melaka’s caretaker chief minister, said the candidates would carry the responsibility of continuing the coalition’s mandate and securing victory at the polls.
fullText: MELAKA: Malaysia’s Barisan Nasional (BN) coalition will announce its candidates for the upcoming Melaka state election on Oct 28, according to the state chairman.
Ab Rauf Yusoh, who is also Melaka’s caretaker chief minister, said the candidates would carry the responsibility of continuing the coalition’s mandate and securing victory at the polls.
The announcement was made at the launch of BN’s election machinery for the Tangga Batu parliamentary constituency in Sungai Udang on Saturday (Oct 17).
On Friday, Ab Rauf said BN’s election preparations had entered their final stage, including negotiations with other parties to finalise electoral cooperation and seat allocations.
"The outcome will be made known following the final round of negotiations, which will take place soon," he said, as quoted by local media platform, The Star.
Polling for the Melaka state election is scheduled for Nov 14, with nomination day on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.
Nearly 700,000 voters in Melaka are set to cast their ballots in the state polls.
Ab Rauf had announced the official dissolution of the state legislative assembly on Sep 23, paving the way for an election that was otherwise due by February 2027.

Before the dissolution, the state government was led by BN, which won 21 of the 28 seats in the 2021 state election, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured five seats and Perikatan Nasional (PN) claimed two seats.

PH joined the state government in 2023 when Ab Rauf became chief minister and reshuffled the executive council to reflect the PH-BN partnership at the federal level following the 2022 general election that had resulted in a hung parliament.
PH however withdrew its support for the state government in July in protest against a constitutional amendment allowing for the appointment of nominated assemblymen.
The upcoming polls in Melaka come just months after BN’s landslide victories in the Negeri Sembilan and Johor state elections.
It won 25 of 36 seats in Negeri Sembilan on Aug 1 as part of a pact with the opposition PN, and 48 of 56 seats in the Johor state election in July where it had contested solo.
